key_insight: Randomized Hadamard transform (HD) can achieve the same provable quantization guarantees as dense random rotations but in O(d log d) time, giving fast, theoretically-backed vector compression.
problem_solved: Closes the gap between empirically effective HD-based quantization and rigorous error guarantees (previously only attainable with costly Θ(d^2) dense rotations).
method: Preprocess vectors with a randomized sign diagonal D and the fast Hadamard matrix H to spread information across coordinates, then apply cheap scalar quantization.
Develop new analysis techniques for the discrete structure of HD to prove concentration and distortion bounds comparable to dense random rotations.
Provide algorithms and complexity analysis that yield O(d log d) runtime with provable bit-rate vs. distortion tradeoffs for common ML tasks.
impact: Delivers fast, memory- and compute-efficient compression with theoretical error guarantees — useful for similarity search, KV-cache/model compression, and federated learning where latency and bandwidth matter.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input vector → randomized sign (D) → Hadamard transform (H) → scalar quantizer → compressed representation
Complexity vs. accuracy chart: compare Θ(d^2) dense rotations and O(d log d) HD runtime with matched distortion curves
Guarantee sketch: pictorial concentration band showing provable error bounds for HD vs. prior empirical uncertainty
Application icons: similarity search, federated learning, KV cache, with arrows indicating reduced latency/bandwidth
paper_title: Provable Quantization with Randomized Hadamard Transform
paper_authors: Ying Feng, Piotr Indyk, Michael Kapralov, Dmitry Krachun, Boris Prokhorov
